stem: What is the central idea of the passage?
correct: Green roofs can cool cities and save energy, even though they cost more to build.

replace.old: A tar roof can become hot enough to cook an egg.
replace.new: A tar roof can become hot enough to cook an egg, and nothing else is true about roofs.

replace.old: Sweat helps people stay cool on hot days.
replace.new: Sweat helps people stay cool on hot days, and roofs have nothing to do with it.

replace.old: Cities should stop building new buildings.
replace.new: Cities should stop building new buildings, because buildings make the city hot.

stem: Which sentence best states a theme of “The Seed Swap”?
correct: Caring well for a few things can be better than having too many.

replace.old: Tomatoes grow better than beans in the summer.
replace.new: Tomatoes grow better than beans in the summer, when the sun is hot.

replace.old: Gardens need sunshine more than water.
replace.new: Gardens need sunshine more than water to grow.

stem: What can the reader infer about Samir?
correct: He is disappointed but keeps working and still helps others.

replace.old: He is angry at Nadia and wants her to fail.
replace.new: He is angry at Nadia and wants her to fail the test at school.

replace.old: He plans to quit the orchestra after the concert.
replace.new: He plans to quit the orchestra after the big concert is over.

replace.old: He does not care where his name is on the list.
replace.new: He does not care where his name is on the list at all.

stem: Why did Hilltop Farm pick only a few baskets of apples that fall?
correct: The bug spray drove away the bees that carry pollen.

replace.old: Worms ate most of the apples on the trees.
replace.new: Worms ate most of the apples on the trees that year.

replace.old: The farmer planted clover between the trees.
replace.new: The farmer planted clover between the trees that spring.

replace.old: The trees were too old to grow fruit.
replace.new: The trees were too old to grow fruit at all.
